comparator.name: French Language and Culture
comparator.academicYear: Latest target-specific official curriculum (2025-2026), checked against the live 2026-2027 catalogue on 2026-10-07
comparator.sourceNotes: Leiden's latest published target-specific study guide identifies a three-year, 180-EC French Language and Culture bachelor centred on French proficiency, linguistics, literature and cultural study. The fully fixed 60-EC first year combines advanced French, oral comprehension and expression, grammar, phonology, French linguistics, literary studies across periods and French cultural history. The upper years continue written and oral French to C1, syntax, Francophone literatures and societies, modern literature, poetry and theatre, research methodology, programme seminars and a 10-EC thesis, while preserving 30 EC of genuine free-choice space. The official programme brochure confirms that teaching is conducted in French and that the programme develops specialist knowledge of French language, literature and culture in France and the wider Francophone world. No formal route or specialisation is required for the generic normalized target; alternating seminars are represented as programme seminar space rather than filled with an invented choice.

components.name: Year 1: French language, linguistics, literature and culture foundations
components.note: Fixed first-year curriculum: advanced French; oral expression and comprehension; grammar and French structure; phonology and word formation; introductions to linguistics and literary studies; medieval, Renaissance-to-Enlightenment, modern and contemporary literature; and French cultural history.

components.name: Years 2-3: advanced French and programme-specific study
components.note: Advanced written and oral French through C1, French syntax, contemporary culture and society, Francophone literatures, modern novels, poetry and theatre, research methodology, philosophy of science and required French-programme seminars, including research seminars.

components.name: Free-choice space
components.note: Genuine third-year minor or elective-package space preserved from the official curriculum.

components.name: BA final thesis
components.note: Independent final research project in French language, linguistics, literature or culture.

programmes.label: French Language and Culture at Leiden University

exception.reason: Leiden French Language and Culture is a cumulative French-medium language-and-humanities degree. Its defining compulsory formation integrates sustained advanced French speaking, listening and academic writing through C1 with grammar, syntax, phonology, French linguistics, literature across historical periods, French and Francophone cultural history, programme-specific research seminars and a French-focused thesis. UCR offers strong English-medium courses in literary, communication, film, media, historical and cultural analysis plus one psycholinguistics course, but it has no taught French-language acquisition sequence and no French or Francophone studies curriculum. A 24-course UCR pathway could study literature, media, identity and postcolonial questions comparatively, but it could not preserve the target's academic identity as French Language and Culture.
exception.curriculumContext: The official curriculum accounts for the full 180 EC as 60 EC of fixed first-year French language, linguistics, literature and culture study; 80 EC of upper-year programme-specific language and humanities formation; 30 EC of genuine free-choice space; and a 10-EC BA thesis. The current cohort rules require multiple French-programme seminars, including research seminars, alongside advanced written and oral language work. Leiden's official programme material states that classes are French-medium and foregrounds the Francophone world beyond France. Even after the 30-EC free-choice block is preserved, the remaining 150 EC form a connected French-proficiency and French/Francophone-studies core rather than a collection of general humanities electives.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCLITR212 Life & Travel Writing, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide substantial comparative literary study. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning adds linguistic and close-reading methods; HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies language acquisition, use and comprehension; and the communication, film, media, history, sociology and heritage offerings support analysis of culture, identity, colonialism, decolonial critique and representation. The workbook nevertheless contains no French-language course at any level, no staged speaking, listening, grammar, phonetics or academic-writing sequence in French, no French linguistics, no historical sequence in French literature, no dedicated French or Francophone cultural-studies course, no French-medium research seminar and no French-focused thesis. Psycholinguistics is a general cognitive-science course rather than language instruction, and the literature and media courses are comparative English-medium offerings rather than a French/Francophone disciplinary spine. No academically honest 24-course closest match can therefore supply the target programme's cumulative language proficiency and area-specific formation.
